alignments.note: Waw of the consecutive form takes the ASV's connective (rule 14).
Finite verb with its English subject pronoun; head on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).
The preposition of אמר ל is rendered by *unto* (rule 11).
Pronominal suffix realized by the object pronoun (rule 18).
Imperative rendered by the bare English imperative.
Paragogic/cohortative he, no English realization (rule 32); MACULA tags it Sh, not Sd.
Dative לְ recast as a bare English indirect object *give me*, leaving the preposition no word (rule 40).
Suffix takes the pronoun the recasting writes for it (rules 18, 40).
Hebrew has no indefinite article, so *a* belongs to the noun it determines (rule 15).

One subordinating morpheme rendered by the fixed pair *for that*; both words are that morpheme's single rendering (rules 30, 55). Headed on *for*; heading on *that* was the competing reading, since either word can realize כִּי.

The Hebrew writes a bare noun with no preposition; the ASV's recasting *set me in the land* supplies *in* for that nominal's own case-function, so it belongs to the noun (rule 33). The construct takes the supplied *the*, the rectum's article taking the written one before its own word (rule 29). The margin's *given me the land of the South* was read and set aside under rule 38.
Article on the nomen rectum takes the *the* standing before its own word; nothing is fronted, since the ASV renders the rectum arthrously (rule 29).
The construct relation's *of* belongs to the nomen rectum, headed on the noun (rules 19, 24).
Finite verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary; head on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).
Object suffix realized by *me* (rule 18).
The waw is rendered by the postposed *also*, which English writes after the verb; the unit is discontinuous rather than broken (rules 25, 51).
Verb rendered by the bare English verb.
Dative לְ left with no English word by the bare indirect object *give me* (rule 40).
Suffix takes the written pronoun (rules 18, 40).
Construct noun takes only its own word, the chain's relation going to the rectum (rule 19).
Nomen rectum with the chain's *of*, headed on the noun (rules 19, 24).
Waw of the consecutive form takes *And* (rule 14).
Finite verb; the explicit subject Caleb takes its own unit.
The dative preposition is left unrendered by the bare English indirect object *gave her* (rule 40).
Suffix realized by *her* (rules 18, 40).
Explicit subject noun.
The object marker has no English of its own; the ASV writes the object bare (rule 16).
No article morpheme stands on the noun, so the supplied *the* determines the nominal expression and joins the noun's unit, discontinuous around the attributive (rules 15, 25).
Attributive adjective keeps its own word.
Coordinating waw takes the written *and* (rule 14).
Second object marker, likewise unrendered (rule 16).
Supplied determiner joins the noun it determines, the unit discontinuous around the attributive (rules 15, 25).
Attributive adjective keeps its own word.

review_notes: The two marginal notes (*Or, present*; *Or, given me the land of the South*) were read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
*in* before *the land* is supplied for a bare Hebrew noun and is placed on that noun under rule 33 rather than on the verb, since *set* already reaches its own object *me*.
The *also* of *give me also springs* answers to the waw of וְנָתַתָּה rather than being `added`, the ASV writing no *and* for it (rule 51).
